name: step1-expiry-coverage
notes: STEP 1 of the three-step data selection: tradable dates per expiry horizon. Inputs are a ticker (foreach.keys) and one prepared option-panel source (pipeline.source.params). For each ticker it counts, per exact calendar DTE 1..45, the distinct entry dates that have a listed expiry and a settled underlying close, keeps the full table (carry.json coverage__<t>.records) plus a chart (artifacts/coverage_figure__<t>/coverage.png), and names the argmax DTE (winner__<t>.records): most dates, ties to the shorter DTE. 'Listed' is what the panel holds: index panels, an expiry in the quoted chain with a valid bid/ask; AMZN, observed option trade/quote rows from the saved 30-45 nominal-DTE archive, where trade bars (price_basis trade_close) are a DECLARED stand-in for tradable quotes and DTEs 1-29 were never collected. 'Settled' is terminal_return not null: the underlying close at settlement is known. There is NO implied-CDF filter; any option the optimizer may trade counts, and a missing CDF is a step-2 gap. The close source is the panel's one source: for AMZN the saved Alpaca IEX daily stock bars (single-exchange closes, NOT the consolidated official close), blocked until ADR-0216's pinned-archive reader lands. selected.jsonl holds one winner row per ticker for step 2, which reads the DTE from it and never types one. Historical coverage is not a prospective calendar policy; nothing is trained or built here.

source.notes: THE DATA SOURCE: the onboarded prepared option panel, named by root/source/stream and resolved from the working directory. Another panel changes these values and nothing else. Both child runbooks onboard their own panel under these same names (index_options reuses its cdf-horizon-source acquisition; stock_options imports the AMZN panel there), so this file runs unchanged from either child. key_fields is the panel's row identity: rows that differ only elsewhere (AMZN rows differing only by price_basis) collide and refuse loudly instead of one being chosen silently. ts_out is quote_date_ms, not the default asof_ms, because the AMZN panel already carries asof_ms and ObservationRows refuses to overwrite a field.

params.provenance_waiver: each winner row carries its own symbol; the key check proves no ticker appears twice

selection_rows.notes: One winner row per ticker: its symbol, selected exact DTE and that DTE's date, forecast and expiry counts and entry-date bounds.

params.source: One winner row per ticker: the selected exact DTE and its date counts; step 2 imports it through source-step1-selection.json

selection_evidence.notes: The step-1 to step-2 hand-off. No expect: the row count is the number of tickers in foreach.keys. The parent directory must exist (mkdir -p) and the writer refuses to overwrite, so to repeat a run move pipeline_runs/step1-expiry-coverage (and step1-selection-source, step2-feature-availability) aside first.

foreach.notes: The only ticker setting: one or several symbols present in the prepared panel. AMZN is ["AMZN"], run from children/stock_options. One shared acquisition is read once and each ticker gets an independent table and argmax; no per-ticker copies of this file exist or are needed.

cohort.notes: Settled rows of this ticker inside the owner's 1-45 day window. A pending row (no terminal_return) or a non-session row (null DTE) is not a tradable date yet and drops out here.

coverage.notes: The full per-DTE table (at most 45 rows per ticker), retained in carry.json. A DTE with no dates is absent, which means zero within this source. listed_forecasts counts panel rows; entry-ms bounds are UTC midnight of the quote dates, not publication clocks.

tie_break.notes: Deterministic argmax: the shortest exact DTE among equal largest date counts. An empty cohort refuses through the missing maximum reference.

winner.notes: The selected DTE's coverage row; collected into selected.jsonl.

params.title: $each
params.xlabel: Exact calendar days to settlement close
params.ylabel: Distinct entry dates (listed expiry, settled close)

coverage_figure.notes: Run-local chart of the whole date-count distribution next to the table, not a fitted return CDF.
